    <div class="pkg-title">
      <h1>Rfishmorph</h1>
      <p class="tagline">Digitizing, storing, analysing and exploring the FISHMORPH database of freshwater fish morphology.</p>
      <div class="badges"><span class="badge-pill blue"><span>version</span><span>0.13.1</span></span><span class="badge-pill grey"><span>R</span><span>≥ 4.1.0</span></span><span class="badge-pill grey"><span>license</span><span>GPL-3</span></span><span class="badge-pill grey"><span>depends</span><span>base R only</span></span></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="pkg-layout">
    <div class="pkg-main">

      <h2>Overview</h2>
      <p><code>Rfishmorph</code> collects the FISHMORPH routines originally developed inside
      <a href="Rpackages_intraitr.html">intraitR</a> into a stand-alone package dedicated to the
      <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/geb.13395" target="_blank">FISHMORPH</a> morphological database of freshwater fishes
      (Brosse <em>et al.</em> 2021). It reconstructs the 21 FISHMORPH landmarks, computes the 11 body segments and the
      9 dimensionless morphological ratios, standardizes landmark geometry and enforces the FISHMORPH digitizing
      conventions, projects specimens into the FISHMORPH functional trait space, and provides visualization and
      quality-control tools to compare segment- and landmark-derived measurements. A guided workflow adds new species,
      using <code>rfishbase</code> to validate taxonomy and build a global list of freshwater fishes.</p>
      <p>Three Shiny applications cover the ends of the workflow: a <strong>guided digitizer</strong> that turns
      specimen photographs into landmarks, an <strong>explorer of the global morphological space</strong> of freshwater
      fishes, and a <strong>drainage-basin explorer</strong> that reads that space through a world map of basins, their
      species composition and their functional-diversity indices.</p>

      <h2>The FISHMORPH scheme</h2>
      <table class="scheme-table">
        <tr><td>21 landmarks</td><td>anatomical points digitized on a lateral photograph (+ scale bar)</td><td><code>fishmorph_schema()$landmark_labels</code></td></tr>
        <tr><td>11 segments</td><td><code>Bl, Bd, Hd, Eh, Mo, PFi, PFl, Ed, Jl, CPd, CFd</code></td><td><code>fishmorph_segment_names()</code></td></tr>
        <tr><td>9 ratios</td><td><code>BEl, VEp, REs, OGp, RMl, BLs, PFv, PFs, CPt</code></td><td><code>fishmorph_ratio_names()</code></td></tr>
      </table>
      <p>Ratios are dimensionless (each is a quotient of two segments of the same specimen), hence scale-invariant and
      comparable across studies.</p>

      <h2>Installation</h2>
      <p>The core functions depend only on base R. Optional features use <code>ggplot2</code> (plots),
      <code>rfishbase</code> (taxonomy / freshwater list), <code>readxl</code>/<code>writexl</code> (Excel I/O),
      <code>shiny</code>/<code>jpeg</code>/<code>png</code> (digitizer), <code>DBI</code>/<code>duckdb</code>/<code>arrow</code>
      (database and archives) and <code>sf</code>/<code>leaflet</code> (basin explorer).</p>
<pre><code># install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("FunTraits/Rfishmorph")

library(Rfishmorph)</code></pre>

      <h2>Typical workflows</h2>
      <h3>1. Measure a specimen</h3>
<pre><code>lm  &lt;- read_landmarks_csv(
  system.file("extdata", "example_landmarks.csv", package = "Rfishmorph"))
seg &lt;- fishmorph_segments(lm, scale_cm = 1)   # 11 segments (cm)
rat &lt;- fishmorph_ratios(seg)                  # 9 ratios
plot_landmarks(lm, specimen = 1)              # points + segments</code></pre>

      <h3>2. Functional trait space</h3>
<pre><code>ref &lt;- load_fishmorph_reference()             # bundled 400-species sample
ts  &lt;- fishmorph_trait_space(ref, groups = ref$Order)   # frozen PCA
plot_trait_space(ts, style = "none", arrows = TRUE)

proj &lt;- project_fishmorph(specimens, reference = ref)   # focal individuals
plot(proj, style = "hull")                    # density heatmap + species hulls
plot(proj, style = "spider", itv_reference = TRUE)</code></pre>

      <h3>3. Quality control: segments vs landmarks</h3>
<pre><code>cmp &lt;- compare_segments_landmarks(landmarks = lm, published = published_segments,
                                  id_col = "Genus.species")
summary(cmp)
plot_segment_landmark_agreement(cmp, type = "scatter")

check_infinite_ratios(rat)          # zero-denominator / outlier ratios
check_geometry_conventions(lm)      # departure from the 5 digitizing rules</code></pre>

      <h3>4. Add a new species</h3>
<pre><code>validate_species_names(c("Salmo trutta", "Esox_lucius"))   # needs rfishbase
rec  &lt;- new_fishmorph_species("Genus novus", segments = list(Bl = 10, Bd = 3.2, ...),
                              family = "Cyprinidae", order = "Cypriniformes")
ref2 &lt;- add_fishmorph_species(ref, rec)
fw   &lt;- freshwater_fish_list()                              # global freshwater list</code></pre>

      <h3>5. Digitize, store safely, explore</h3>
      <p>Photographs stay on your machine: only their file name and pixel dimensions are ever recorded.</p>
<pre><code>launch_fishmorph_digitizer(xlsx_path = "FISHMORPH_PUBLI_9556sp.xlsx",
                           photo_dir = "Photos", operator = "AT", mode = "new")

jdir &lt;- "landmark_journal"
fm_journal_status(jdir)                       # what is in the journal?
base &lt;- fishmorph_consolidate(jdir)           # wide table, one row per key
qc   &lt;- fishmorph_journal_qc(jdir)            # never-verified points, gaps

res  &lt;- fishmorph_build_db(jdir, db_path = "fishmorph.duckdb",
                           export_dir = "exports")        # Parquet + CSV
con  &lt;- fishmorph_db_connect("fishmorph.duckdb")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "FROM v_ratios WHERE species = ?", params = list("Coilia.nasus"))

launch_fishmorph_space()                      # global morphospace, 9 556 species
launch_fishmorph_basins()                     # drainage-basin explorer</code></pre>

      <h2>Data architecture</h2>
      <div class="flow">
        <div class="flow-box"><b>Photographs</b>local only</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
        <div class="flow-box"><b>Append-only journal</b>source of truth, one TSV per session</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
        <div class="flow-box"><b>DuckDB database</b>integrity constraints, views, SQL</div>
        <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
        <div class="flow-box"><b>Parquet / CSV</b>citable archive</div>
      </div>
      <p>Digitizing never overwrites what is already written. The journal is the only durable layer; the database and
      the workbook are derived artefacts that <code>fishmorph_build_db()</code> rebuilds from scratch in seconds. Each
      point carries a <code>status</code> (<code>placed</code>, <code>seeded</code>, <code>derived</code>, <code>na</code>)
      that a wide coordinate table cannot express — filter on it before any validation analysis.</p>

      <div class="callout">
        <strong>Round-trip guarantee.</strong> <code>reconstruct_fishmorph_landmarks()</code> is the inverse of
        <code>fishmorph_segments()</code>: the free placement parameters change only <em>where</em> landmarks sit, never
        the segment <em>lengths</em>. <code>check_reconstruction_roundtrip()</code> verifies that
        segments → landmarks → segments returns the input to machine precision.
      </div>

        <tr><td>Shiny applications</td>
            <td><code>launch_fishmorph_digitizer()</code> <code>launch_fishmorph_reconstructor()</code>

<script>
const CORRECT_HASH = "ac95cc34e3ff9d4e59fd3066f6feaee0d2f4f7f97d3865148bc5767834883ff5";

async function sha256(msg) {
  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(msg));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2,"0")).join("");
}

function unlock() {
  document.getElementById("pw-overlay").style.display = "none";
  document.getElementById("pkg-content").style.display = "block";
  sessionStorage.setItem("rpackages_unlocked", "1");
}

async function checkPw() {
  const hash = await sha256(document.getElementById("pw-input").value);
  if (hash === CORRECT_HASH) {
    unlock();
  } else {
    const err = document.getElementById("pw-error");
    err.textContent = "Incorrect password. Please try again.";
    document.getElementById("pw-input").value = "";
    document.getElementById("pw-input").focus();
    setTimeout(() => { err.textContent = ""; }, 3000);
  }
}

if (sessionStorage.getItem("rpackages_unlocked") === "1" ||
    sessionStorage.getItem("rscripts_unlocked") === "1") {
  unlock();
}

</script>
